summary.headline: Astronomy’s Universal Use and Honor
summary.text: Defense of astronomy as the mistress of the sciences, detailing its applications to zodiacal regions, timekeeping, agriculture, travel, politics, warfare, medicine, dreams, kings’ campaigns, espionage, harvests, and horoscopic judgment. The treatise then argues that foreknowledge of future things is divinely reserved or attained only through spiritual purification and arduous study of the stars’ motions and configurations.
